name: UiPath, Inc.

profile.description: UiPath provides an enterprise automation platform combining robotic process automation, process mining and agentic AI orchestration (Maestro). Fiscal 2026 revenue was $1.61B (+13%) with ARR of $1.85B; Q2 FY2027 revenue was $410M (+13%) with ARR of $1.94B (+12%), net retention of 107% and a fourth consecutive GAAP-profitable quarter [1].

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): UiPath extended from RPA into process mining, document understanding and a 'Platform for Agentic Automation' anchored by Maestro, growing ARR to $1.94B (+12%) [1]. AI Deployment (2/2): agentic automation products ship to enterprise customers with 107% dollar-based net retention and ARR above $1.9B [1]. Market Share (1/2): the recognized RPA leader, but employees and analysts note 'everybody does agentic AI' and GenAI is pressuring the category [2]. Pipeline (1/2): Maestro and agent products are named, but dated roadmaps with revenue visibility are limited. R&D Intensity (1/1): software R&D spend of roughly a quarter of revenue is above the sector average.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): the stated mission to 'accelerate human achievement' through automation is clear but not distinctive among enterprise software peers [2]. Community Impact (1/2): UiPath publishes an annual Impact Report with Responsible AI, AI-skills training and sustainability programs, but no dollar-quantified distinctive initiative was found [3]. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor shows 3.2/5 for senior management, 'incompetent management' appears in 48 reviews and a partner leader says the new co-CEO 'fired good executives and workers' [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): no meaningful net insider buying was found.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as Growth on available metrics (PEG unavailable, excluded). D/E 4.1% (1.0), ROE 20.0% (1.0, 2x), profit margin 21.0% (1.0), revenue growth 13.4% YoY (1.0), ~12% 5-yr revenue CAGR (1.0, 2x) and forward P/E 14.2 (1.0) all meet or beat target [1]. Average volume of 67.9M shares at $13.12 gives ~$890M daily dollar volume, clearing the liquidity floor. Weighted score 10.0/10.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (4/9): UiPath is both enabler and target of AI; the automation category faces direct substitution pressure from LLM-based agents from hyperscalers and model labs, and employees describe 'AI eating our lunch' and 'everybody does agentic AI, it's not a differentiator' [2]. Enterprise governance, integrations and installed-base switching costs provide partial protection, and growth is holding at 12-13% ARR. AI Opportunity (1/1): agentic automation and Maestro are shipping products within a $1.94B ARR base [1].

infinite_game.summary: UiPath has a founder-led automation vision and has adapted from RPA toward agentic AI, but the change is incremental and defensive against GenAI pressure. Mixed employee sentiment, leadership turnover and a 'win the agentic category' posture lead Sinek to read the company as playing more to defend a category than to advance an enduring cause.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'a robot for every person' evolved into 'accelerate human achievement', a purpose statement that reads as product marketing rather than a cause that has shaped costly decisions [2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): founder Daniel Dines returned as CEO in June 2024, giving continuity, but 3.2/5 senior-management ratings, 'bad leadership' reviews and executive turnover show a mixed circle of safety [2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): positioning around being the agentic leader against Microsoft, ServiceNow and model labs is framed around category defense rather than learning, and staff say agentic AI is not a differentiator [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): UiPath is moving from attended RPA to an agentic orchestration platform, an incremental extension of its automation core rather than abandonment of a profitable model [1][2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): reinvesting in an agentic platform while reaching GAAP profitability shows a long-term bet, but cost discipline and reorganizations have also been used to defend margins [1][2].

investment_thesis: UiPath at $13.12 (about $6.8B market cap) trades at 14.2x forward earnings and 19.6x trailing with a 21.0% profit margin, 20.0% ROE and virtually no leverage (D/E 4.1%) [1]. ARR of $1.94B is growing 12%, net retention is 107%, Q2 FY2027 revenue grew 13% and the company has posted four consecutive GAAP-profitable quarters, while Maestro-led agentic automation gives it a credible position in enterprise AI orchestration [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that LLM agents commoditize RPA: ARR growth is stuck at 11-12%, net retention of 107% is modest, and staff and analysts describe the category as pressured by generative AI with agentic capability no longer a differentiator [2]. Glassdoor shows 3.2/5 senior-management ratings, executive turnover under the new co-CEO structure, and no insider buying, and the stock is below its 50-day average ($14.59) [2]. The Inspire score of 62 is Aligned but carries no weight in the score.
key_catalysts: Maestro and agentic automation products converting the $1.94B ARR base into higher net retention than the current 107% [1]
Sustained GAAP profitability (four consecutive quarters) and free cash flow supporting buybacks and a re-rating from 14.2x forward earnings [1]
Enterprise demand for governed, auditable agent orchestration across the installed base as GenAI pilots move to production [1][2]
key_risks: AI substitution: hyperscaler and model-lab agents compete directly with RPA and orchestration, and 'everybody does agentic AI' limits pricing power [2]
Growth stuck near 12% ARR with 107% net retention, leaving little cushion if enterprise IT budgets tighten [1]
Leadership and culture risk: 3.2/5 senior-management rating, executive churn under the co-CEO structure and low retention evidence [2]
